key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the best task-specific predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks offered strong shared-learning performance across related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a generalizable multi-output model and a more accurate task-specific ensemble when predicting key joint quality metrics.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers, task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Used a shared welding dataset to predict UTS, weld bead hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated models with RMSE and R² for each target.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² for all three targets, while MTNN still showed solid generalization across the related prediction tasks.
watch_item: The reported advantage of stacking may depend on dataset size and distribution, so external validation is needed before deployment on new welding conditions.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
